interest: Shows SCAP pressure to end Hokkaido's kangoku-beya debt-peonage coal mine system, exposed by press and advisory committee reports.
overview: January 1947 memo: Mulliken tells Hilldring that press reports (Christian Science Monitor, Allied Labor News, Asahi) exposed the kangoku-beya debt-peonage system holding 10,000-12,000 Hokkaido coal miners under armed guard; after SCAP's Stanchfield confirmed conditions, Mulliken recommends a formal query to SCAP to speed reform.

subfiles.about: A memorandum recommending that an inquiry be sent to SCAP regarding slave labor conditions and debt peonage in Hokkaido coal mines.
subfiles.summary: Mulliken's memo details the kangoku-beya system holding 10,000-12,000 indebted Hokkaido coal miners under armed guard with police complicity, per press reports; a provincial raid freed about 2,000 but failed to prosecute mine bosses, so Mulliken, backed by SCAP's Stanchfield, urges a State telegram pressing SCAP to act.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from Mr. Mulliken to General Hilldring regarding Contract Labor in Hokkaido Coal Mines
